description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a beloved Middle Eastern comfort food, cherished for its simplicity and deeply satisfying flavors. This hearty and wholesome soup combines tender red lentils with aromatic spices, fresh vegetables, and a bright squeeze of lemon. It is a perfect, nourishing meal for any day, offering warmth and traditional taste in every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear, then drain them well. Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and finely dice the carrot and potato, ensuring all pieces are roughly the same size for even cooking.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic, diced carrot, and diced potato, cooking for another 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.

instructions.title: Add Lentils and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the rinsed lentils, ground cumin, and turmeric powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and coat the lentils, enhancing their flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender and the soup has thickened. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Season and Blend (Optional)
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. For a smoother consistency, use an immersion blender to blend a portion of the soup directly in the pot, or transfer half of the soup to a regular blender, blend until smooth, and return it to the pot. Leave some texture for a more rustic soup.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference. Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley before serving.

tips: Always rinse your red lentils thoroughly before cooking to remove any impurities and ensure a clear, flavorful broth.
For extra depth of flavor, toast the cumin and turmeric briefly with the aromatics before adding liquid. This brings out their essential oils.
The soup thickens as it cools. If reheating, you might need to add a splash of water or broth to reach your desired consistency. Always finish with a fresh squeeze of lemon.
article:
The aroma of simmering lentils, fragrant with garlic and lemon, is a quintessential scent in many Middle Eastern homes. Among the vast array of comforting soups and stews from the region, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known affectionately as Adas, stands out as a true culinary gem. This simple yet profoundly satisfying dish is a staple, cherished for its nourishing qualities, ease of preparation, and incredible flavor. Whether you're seeking a hearty meal on a chilly evening, a wholesome lunch, or a taste of authentic Lebanese tradition, Adas delivers warmth and comfort in every spoonful. It's a testament to how humble ingredients can create something extraordinary, offering a glimpse into the heart of Middle Eastern hospitality and home cooking.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a beloved vegan soup deeply rooted in Middle Eastern cuisine, particularly in Lebanon. It's renowned for its vibrant orange-red hue, creamy texture, and bright, tangy flavor profile. At its core, Adas is a very simple soup, typically made from red lentils, onions, garlic, and often carrots or potatoes, all simmered together until tender and then blended to a smooth consistency. What truly elevates Adas is the generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice added at the end, which cuts through the richness of the lentils and brightens every bite. A drizzle of olive oil and a sprinkle of dried mint are common finishing touches, adding layers of traditional flavor. Beyond its delicious taste, Adas is incredibly nutritious, packed with plant-based protein, fiber, and essential vitamins and minerals, making it a wholesome choice for any meal. Its affordability and quick cooking time also contribute to its widespread popularity, especially during the colder months or during the fasting month of Ramadan.

## Ingredients You Need for Adas

The beauty of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup lies in its reliance on simple, pantry-friendly ingredients that come together to create a complex and satisfying flavor. Here's what you'll typically need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Make sure they are split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily, contributing to the soup's creamy texture.
*   **Onion:** A medium yellow or white onion, finely chopped, forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** Several cloves, minced, add depth and pungency.
*   **Carrot (optional but recommended):** One medium carrot, diced, adds a touch of sweetness and enhances the soup's color and nutritional value.
*   **Potato (optional):** A small potato, peeled and diced, can add extra body and creaminess.
*   **Olive Oil:** Used for sautéing the aromatics and as a finishing drizzle.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** The liquid base for the soup. Broth will add more flavor.
*   **Cumin:** Ground cumin is essential, providing that characteristic earthy, warm Middle Eastern spice.
*   **Salt and Black Pepper:** To taste, adjusting as needed throughout the cooking process.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for balancing the flavors and adding a bright, tangy finish.
*   **Dried Mint (optional but highly recommended):** Crushed and sprinkled over the finished soup for an authentic touch.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Making a delicious batch of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is surprisingly straightforward. Follow these steps for a comforting and flavorful result:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it. If using, add the diced carrot and potato and sauté for a few minutes.
3.  **Add Lentils and Spices:** Stir in the rinsed red lentils, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and coat the lentils.
4.  **Simmer:** Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have mostly broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional but Recommended):** For a smooth, creamy soup, carefully use an immersion blender directly in the pot to blend the soup until it reaches your desired consistency. Alternatively, you can transfer batches of the soup to a regular blender (be extremely careful when blending hot liquids) and then return it to the pot. If you prefer a chunkier soup, you can skip this step or mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon.
6.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your preferred consistency. Taste and adjust salt, pepper, and cumin as needed.
7.  **Finish with Lemon:** Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the fresh lemon juice. This step is crucial for the authentic flavor of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with dried mint, if using.

## Pro Tips for the Best Adas Results

Achieving the perfect bowl of Adas is simple, but a few pro tips can elevate your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup from good to absolutely outstanding:

*   **Rinse Those Lentils:** Don't skip rinsing the lentils. It helps remove starch, which can make the soup cloudy, and any small debris.
*   **Toast Your Spices:** Briefly toasting the cumin with the onions and garlic before adding the liquid helps to release its full aroma and deepen its flavor, creating a richer base for your Adas.
*   **Balance the Lemon:** The fresh lemon juice is non-negotiable. Add it at the very end, off the heat, to preserve its bright, fresh flavor. Start with the recommended amount and then add more to taste until you achieve that perfect tangy balance that cuts through the earthiness of the lentils.
*   **Achieve Creamy Texture:** For the creamiest soup, ensure the lentils are thoroughly cooked and soft before blending. An immersion blender is a fantastic tool for this, allowing you to blend directly in the pot. If you don't have one, a regular blender works, but be cautious with hot liquids.
*   **Don't Overcook:** While lentils need to be tender, overcooking can sometimes lead to a slightly mushy or overly thick consistency before blending. Keep an eye on them; 20-25 minutes is usually sufficient.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving. Seasoning can vary based on the broth you use and personal preference. Don't be afraid to add more salt, pepper, or a pinch more cumin if needed.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a wonderfully versatile dish that can be served in many ways, making it suitable for a light lunch, a hearty dinner, or even as a comforting appetizer. Here are some traditional and popular serving suggestions:

*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** Always offer extra lemon wedges on the side. Many people love to add an additional squeeze of fresh lemon juice to their bowl just before eating, enhancing the soup's signature tanginess.
*   **Pita Bread:** Warm pita bread, either whole or torn into pieces, is the perfect accompaniment for scooping up every last drop of the delicious soup. You can also toast pita bread to make crispy "croutons."
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or cilantro adds a burst of freshness and color.
*   **Drizzle of Olive Oil:** A final drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil over each serving not only adds flavor but also a lovely sheen.
*   **Dried Mint:** Crushed dried mint is a classic Lebanese topping that provides a unique, cooling aroma and flavor.
*   **Pickles and Olives:** A small plate of traditional Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips or cucumbers) and olives makes for an authentic and delicious side.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a dash of red pepper flakes or a swirl of chili oil can be added to individual bowls.
*   **On its Own:** Adas is so flavorful and satisfying that it truly shines on its own as a wholesome and complete meal.

## Variations and Substitutions for Adas

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, its simple base makes it incredibly adaptable to various tastes and dietary needs. Don't hesitate to experiment!

*   **Add More Vegetables:** Beyond carrots and potatoes, consider adding finely diced celery, bell peppers, or even a handful of spinach or kale towards the end of cooking for extra nutrients and texture.
*   **Spice It Up:** For a different flavor profile, you could add a pinch of turmeric for extra color and earthy notes, a touch of coriander, or even a dash of cayenne pepper for heat. Smoked paprika can also add a delightful smoky depth.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, fresh mint or cilantro blended into the soup before serving, or used as a garnish, can offer a brighter, fresher taste.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are traditional and ideal for their quick cooking and creamy texture, you could experiment with yellow lentils, though they might take slightly longer to cook and yield a different color.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Adas is naturally gluten-free, provided you use gluten-free vegetable broth.
*   **Oil-Free:** For an oil-free version, sauté the onions and garlic in a splash of water or vegetable broth instead of olive oil.
*   **Protein Boost:** While Adas is a complete protein source on its own, you could add cooked chickpeas or white beans for extra texture and protein, or even some shredded chicken or lamb if you're not keeping it vegetarian/vegan.
*   **Tomato Paste:** A tablespoon of tomato paste can be added with the onions and garlic to deepen the color and add a subtle umami note to the soup.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is more than just a dish; it's a warm hug in a bowl, a testament to the power of simple ingredients, and a delicious journey into the heart of Middle Eastern comfort food. Easy to make, incredibly nutritious, and bursting with flavor, it's a recipe you'll want to revisit again and again. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by this timeless and heartwarming soup.
